subject: Renewal scaling signal — usage, performance, and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jordan@aegishealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal health check + capacity question

Camila —

Hope you had a good weekend. We're starting to prep internally for our August renewal and I pulled together the Q1 usage doc (attached) so you can see what's changed since we last talked. Two things jumped out:

- Token spend is up ~48% q/q as we rolled out embeddings for search fallback; monthly avg tokens now ~2.1B.
- We see periodic latency spikes during M-F 10a-1p PST (up to 600–800ms tail latency on gen endpoints).

We want to understand: are we better off staying on Hosted with a larger commit, or should we move to Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput? We're sensitive to both unit cost and the operational risk of those latency spikes.

Can you share a short ops/ROI recap and 1–2 concrete paths (term/commit + capacity) we could evaluate ahead of renewal? Also flag any quick wins we can implement without contract changes.

Attached: aegis_q1_usage_report.pdf

Thanks — happy to schedule a 30-min sync this week.

—Jordan
Head of Platform, AegisHealth
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal health check + capacity question

Jordan — thanks for the data, useful snapshot. Quick summary from our side after a rapid pass through your Q1:

- Usage: ~2.1B tokens/month with 70% of calls coming from the new embeddings+rerank flow. Median request size increased ~1.8x.
- Cost drivers: embeddings footprint + increase in tail tokens from retries during the 10a-1p window.
- Perf: the latency spikes align with concurrent long-context gen jobs that aren't being batched efficiently.

Three recommended paths (short, actionable):

1) Short-term (no contract change) — tuning & quick wins (2–4 weeks):
   - Prefix caching for your top-50 prompt families (expected 15–25% token reduction).
   - Adjust request routing to prefer lower-latency hardware region during the 10a–1p window.
   - Opt into continuous batching for gen endpoints (no code changes, toggle on our side).

2) Mid-term (12-month renewal, Hosted) — commit + economics:
   - 12-month, 30% commit uplift vs current run-rate ⇒ we can offer a blended unit price that lowers per-token cost ~22% and include a 60-day free pilot of quantized model variants for embeddings.

3) Pilot Dedicated (3-month pilot → full reserved capacity):
   - Reserved pool sized for current 95th percentile gen throughput; expected to eliminate the tail spikes and lower 99th latency by ~40–60ms.
   - Upfront pilot fee is credit against first dedicated invoice. We can run a cost comparison: Hosted with uplift vs Dedicated (showing expected per-token + infra amortization).

I attached our ops summary with a quick ROI table and a first-draft pilot scope. If you want, Ben and Laura can join a technical runthrough. Suggested next step: 30-min call to align on appetite (short-term tuning vs Dedicated pilot).

Attachments: redwood_q1_ops_summary.xlsx; pilot_scope_draft.docx

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal health check + capacity question (technical notes)

Jordan / Camila — quick technical notes from my side ahead of the call:

- Latency spikes look like they're caused by long-gen tasks that never hit prefix cache; if Aegis can provide 4–6 representative prompt families we can lock down which prefixes to cache and validate savings.
- Recommending a trial of int8 quantized embeddings for a subset of calls — expected token-cost parity but ~2–3x throughput improvement on the same hardware (low risk pilot).
- For Dedicated sizing, we'll simulate a 99th-percentile run using your Q1 peak days (I can run the sim if you give access to the usage logs or export).

One ask: Jordan, can you drop the recent usage logs (anonymized) into the Drive link Camila shared? That lets us produce the Dedicated comparison that ties directly to your peaks.

—Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Please send a short SOW + pilot acceptance criteria and a draft amendment we can route to Procurement (we prefer DocuSign).

If you can get the SOW + draft terms over by end of day Monday 4/26 we'll start internal approvals. I'll also upload the anonymized logs to the Drive link today.

Jordan
